E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race
 
OTHER NOTES:
· Helmets are required for all races.
· Please arrive early to check in. Check-in closes 30 minutes prior to start times.

EventNotes:
Join us for an all-day, no-pressure ride on the Shenango River Trail / Towpath. One of PA's most overlooked technical corridors. Not a race, no timing, two-way rider traffic the whole day. Just a good trail and a reason to spend the day on it.

When:
October 11th (10/11, binary, we see you nerds)

Where:
99 W Kidds Mill Rd, Greenville, PA 15164

Map:
https://caltopo.com/m/9TBC19S

Two out-and-back routes, same trailhead.
Short Trip: Kidds Mill to New Hamburg back to Kidds Mill (~8.5-9 mi)
Long Haul: Kidds Mill to Big Bend to Kidds Mill (~17.5 mi)

Natural-surface trail, a few stream crossings, mostly flat with some sudden technical ups and downs. Real terrain, not a paved cruise or flow trail. There's lots of place where you might even need to hike a bike. At least I do. The corridor also sees regular use from local equestrian groups and trail runners.

The trail follows the Shenango River. Pennsylvania's 2021 River of the Year, and hosts numerous kayak races of its own along much of the corridor. Probably going to see some herons, eagles, kingfishers. Nature!

Riders of all skill levels welcome! This is as much about getting people out on the Shenango Trail.

EventName: Falkorburg Cross -- Event #3 of the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series
EventNotes:
Event Name: Falkorburg Cross, Event #3 in the 2026 BikeReg Cyclocross Super Series

Hosted by Baltimore Bicycle Works Racing

When: Sunday October 11th, 2026

Venue: Berg Farm, STM Coaching, Stevenson, MD 

Venue Address: Please follow these coordinates to the parking area, 39°24'47.0"N 76°42'54.5"W, Stevenson, MD 21153.  

Parking & Gear Drop-off: There is limited parking on site at the venue (yellow in the image below), carpooling is encouraged. There will be a gear drop so bikes, gear, and people can be dropped off as close to the action as possible. Navigation to race and the gear drop is best using the following coordinates:  39°24'47.0"N 76°42'54.5"W  Entrance for the drop-off and parking is off of Stevenson Rd. Between Valley Acres Dr. and Old Valley Rd. just past the Stevenson Village Shopping Center. The overflow parking will be at the Stevenson Village Shopping Center itself; however we've never needed to use it. Parking opens at 6:30am.  Draft course map.

 

Gender Equality & Transgender Policy: Classes designated “Masters” are open to Men and Women. Minimum Racing Age and categories quoted are for Men; please see the current USAC Rulebook for minimum Racing Age and categories for Women.  The Super Series  welcomes everyone to participate in the gender category they feel is most appropriate to them, as described in USA Cycling policies: https://usacycling.org/about-us/governance/transgender-athletes-policy.

or

The Venue: The home of Falkorburg Cross, Berg Farm, is nestled in the picturesque valleys of Baltimore County. It features a historic stone barn which holds registration and will shelter anyone looking for cover. As usual we’ll have a food truck and beer garden to keep you fed and hydrated. 

 

RACE DAY FOOD: Get your taste buds ready!

We've got Globe coffee in the morning serving up delicious coffee and some breakfast, then Ryleighs Oyster House will be on site 11am-4pm, we will also have Taharka ice cream and tasty beers available from Peabody Heights.

 

*While usually open to the public, the course will be closed beginning Friday, October 9th for course prep and will re-open on race day.

**Pre-ride opens at 7:30 am on the day of the event with the first race starting at 9:00am.  Warming up on the course during races is not permitted. All USAC rules apply.

 

The Course: The course is located on the Berg Farm in Stevenson, MD. This is a dedicated cyclocross course that is available for practicing throughout most of the year. Waivers are available on-site and required for anyone interested in scouting the course outside of set-up weekend and event day. However, we will have a few tweaks up our sleeves specifically for race day. The terrain is fast and flowing with a number of technical turns and short super punchy climbs. You won’t find any Belgian walls here, but you’ll find plenty of off-camber and twisty turns. 

The flyover is back this year! All fields, adult and junior, will pass over (and under) the flyover. We've added rungs along the left side of both the climb and descent to provide optional additional traction to anyone walking the feature. To walk, run, or ride is a common decision a rider makes when navigating any cyclocross course feature. Please remember to ride within your abilities, stay safe, and keep the rubber side down. 

Rest assured, the balance between power and technical will make this course a leveled playing field.  

 

Spectating:  The venue features easy access to all course locations.  Want to see your favorite rider zoom around the course and navigate the technical turns? No problem! You can enjoy a tasty beverage by team sponsor Peabody Heights Brewer, and watch the ‘cross action’ unfold from one central location or investigate the many prime areas throughout the course for great spectating and friendly heckling. Bring your chair and your ID, and stay around to watch the elite field fly through the course. Bringing the kids? We’ll have 10a.m. and 12p.m. Little Belgians races for the wee little ones age 9 and under. Top it off with food and coffee from local vendors. 

 

Lil Belgians Kids' Races: FREE races for kids ages 9 and under. Helmets are required, a guardian must be present and sign a release (available at the registration tent). NO racing license required. Space is limited to 50 kids, and for everyone's convenience, please pre-register online at https://www.bikereg.com/falkorburg2024 to guarantee your spot.

Registration, Entry Fees, & Licensing:  all registration and payment for this event, including race day registration, will be conducted through BikeReg.  Addtional entries are offered at $20 ($25 on race day) when purchased in the same BikeReg shopping cart.  If the entries are purchased separately during the pre-registration period, contact us for a partial refund; on event day a coupon code will be made available at the day-of registration table to achieve the same discounted price.  Entry fees will increase to $50 for adults and $30 for Junior Men for race day registration (all Junior Women race free this year), to reflect the day-of surcharge.  There will be no in-person sales at the event -- register online, either at home before coming out or on your phone at the event.  You MUST present your racing license (if you have one) or 1-Day receipt in order to be issued a bib, and you should also be prepared to show your confirmation email.  In order to expedite your entry, make sure you have completed the online waiver before approaching the day-of registration table.

This page will re-open for day-of registration by 6 AM;  check-in will open by 7 AM.  Check-in and registration for all races will close 15 minutes prior to the scheduled start of the race.  There will be no exceptions made to this rule -- plan to show up timely for the race you want to enter.

Thanks to our sponsors, U19 Women may race in any class they qualify for by Cyclocross category, but remain eligible for free entry (use code Watch_Out_Boys), if registering for and girls category, there will be no fee (except Mabra charge).  For race day entry, the day-of surcharge will be applied as appropriate.  Any current National Cyclocross Champions shall be granted free entry, but must wear their national jersey in the class in which it was won.

Also thanks to sponsor generosity, BBWR is able offer complimentary entry to the first 10 BIPOC riders who register.  Please use the ‘Contact Us’ link at the bottom of this page to request the coupon code.

 

A USA Cycling racing license is required for entry.  Riders who do not provide a USAC Annual racing license # at registration will be assessed an additional $15 for a Beginner 1-Day license.  This license is valid for entry only in fields that are open to Novice Men, Women, or Non-Binary riders.  For all other fields, you must present proof of an active USAC racing license (or a printed Authorization to Ride) showing your Cyclocross category and Racing Age.

Staging & Call Ups: Cat 5 Men's and Cat 4/5 Women’s races are staged based on pre-registration order. The rest of the races are staged according to Super Series standing for the top 8 positions and then based on CrossResults.com rankings for the remainder of pre-registered riders. Race categories and staging information is available https://www.superseriescx.com/about-1. The "Race Day Schedule" table below also provides staging information. 

 

Points: Points are awarded for Series ranking to the following Super Series categories – Men Cat 1,2,3; Women Cat 1,2,3; Men Cat 3, Men Cat 4; Masters 40+ Cat 1,2,3; Masters 50+ Cat 1,2,3,4; Masters 40+/50+ Cat 3, 4, 5; Singlespeed Men, Singlespeed Women; all U19.; Men Cat 5 and Women Cat 4/5 beginner races are not ranked. Professional chip time results by Insight Timing Services. See the Super Series Website for full details about rules and regulations for series points; https://www.superseriescx.com.

Prizes:

.Mens and Womens Cats 1/2/3 will be awarded prize money!  $300 5 Deep

. All other Adults will receive prizes at the promoter’s discretion; typically 5 deep for Falkorburg Cross.

. Juniors will receive medals three places deep.

. Lil’ Belgians races will have medals and snacks for all.

. Single Speed - The legendary traveling Cat Trophies will be back again for the Men’s and Women’s SSCX races this year. Who will claim the coveted trophy this year and win the rights to host the trophy in their home until next year? Plus podium prizes, 5 deep. 

Team tents: Premium tent spots are available for reservation through BikeReg and include one reserved parking spot near the team tent area (so, yeah…you’re really just paying for primo parking). No reservation? No problem. There’s plenty of room for all at Falkorburg Cross. You can use the drop-off loop for your gear and add your tent to the party. Important: For the 2026 Season USAC is requiring teams setting up a tent in a designated team area (pre-paid tent spaces for Falkorburg Cross), to arrive with proof of USAC Safe Sport Certification Safe Sport Training | USA Cycling. This applies to one individual representative for the team who must be present to gain access to the tent row. This requirement does not apply to all of the first-come, first-serve, unreserved team tents that are set up outside of the premium tent spots. 

 

 

 

Contacts:

FalkorburgCX@gmail.com 

Additional info at: facebook.com/falkorburgcx/ 

and https://baltimorebicycleworksracing.com/falkorburg-cx

EventNotes:
All Proceeds Benefit the East Haddam Land Trust 

The Nutmeg 40 is a unique 40-mile adventure loop that utilizes the most interesting and challenging public preserves in East Haddam, Salem, and Lyme, Connecticut. The most iconic portion of this loop is the The Goodwin Trail. This is a unique, 13.5 mile linear trail that winds its way through preserved lands owned by local land trusts, municipalities, the Yale School of Forestry, and Nehantic State Park.  

Ride begins and ends at Yankee Cider, 23 Petticoat Lane, East Haddam, 06423.  Parking, restrooms, and rider meetings at Yankee Cider, then we will complete a challenging and scenic 40 mile loop traversing as-much-trail as possible . You will be very happy to see Yankee Cider upon the completion of the loop… we promise!  

Everybody who registers before Sept 20, will receive a free, Ronnie Romance designed Nutmeg 40, 2026 t-shirt. We will ask you for your shirt size in the custom question section of the registration.

The course is unmarked, so a navigation device will be required

GPX route will be emailed to registrants the Thursday before the event.

A mountain bike with sturdy tires and low gearing is recommended

Sorry no Ebikes 

Stocked rest stops every 10 miles on the course 

In addition to riding off-road on the Goodwin Trail, cyclists will be riding through The Lena Preserve, The Jewett Preserve, The Johnstone Preserve, and many others that will all blend together in a mind bender of a day out on the bike.

The Goodwin Trail, and the other single tracks you will encounter (while 99 percent rideable) are a technical test of your off-roading skills on a bicycle – this is the longest, most remote mountain bike event in the state, and entrants should be prepared for a physical test/challenge to remember.  This will be a timed race for those who choose to race, and an all day trail adventure for those who want to take it at their own pace.    

This will be a challenging event for many of us. Please give careful consideration before registering. 

We will create rest/refreshment stops along the way. All the snacks will be homemade - probably lots of banana bread. We will have sandwiches, fruit, and goodies at about the ½ way point and hearty vegetarian chili and cornbread at the end at Yankee Cider. A variety of locally made, cold, hard and soft cider will be available at the cash bar upon your return.  You will be well fed this day. Please specify any severe or life-threatening food allergies when you register.  Lastly, we cannot guarantee an allergen-free environment due to shared kitchen facilities.

Pease carry your own water, snacks, and other needed accessories as well.  There are places where a water filter might come in handy.  

Cell service is very inconsistent on the trail. We strongly recommend participating with a buddy or two. We will provide a sweeper who could provide hands-off assistance. Please note that it could take skilled medical/mechanical staff up to two hours to reach you on the trail. 

We will host the event in rain. We will cancel if there are strong storms. Please check the EHLT website and Facebook pages for last minute updates.

Your registration donation will help East Haddam Land Trust preserve and steward land in perpetuity for all of us to enjoy, and earn you a 1-year membership to EHLT. Your membership entitles you to advanced notice to our hikes, paddles, and other fun events as well as allowing you to participate in members-only experiences. We are grateful for your help. 

Please note that if this event is cancelled for any reason, we will continue to accept your donation to EHLT and not issue refunds. Thank you for understanding this.

Please sign the online waiver form before you arrive.

Please arrive to Yankee Cider, 23 Petticoat Lane, East Haddam, CT 06423 from 7:30am- 8:15am. We will host a short meeting for all cyclists at 8:15am then those who are racing will leave followed by the recreational cyclists. 

Please learn about the Eightmile River Watershed, which hosts the Goodwin Trail, and find trail maps here:

https://www.eightmileriver.org/outdoor-recreation/
PresentedBy: East Haddam Land Trust and Ron's Bikes

EventNotes:
Basic Information: Recreational Bicycle Ride “Cherry Lake Challenge”   10/11/2026 

 

Date: Sunday October 11 2026

Location: Start/Finish  Downtown Tuolumne, CA  (Bay at Cherry Valley Blvd N)

Set Up Time:  6 a.m. to 8 A.M.

Event Time:  7:30 a.m. to 4 p.m.

Breakdown Time:   4 p.m. to 6 p.m.

 

Note: This info has been edited with more road info,  total climbing info and expected  temperatures (cool)

Type of Event:    Bicycle rides (not races) out to Cherry Lake and back, all on pavement with two routes:

                “A” Ride (Short):Tuolumne to Reed Creek (just to the east, at 1N04 and 3N01) and back   (45 miles) approx 6,000 feet of total climbing. Lowpoint 2200, Highpoint 4970

                “B” Ride (Long) Tuolumne to Cherry Lake and back including loop south to Cherry Oil Rd  (74 miles) approx 7800 feet of total climbing. Lowpoint  2200, Highpoint 5600

                Temperatures should range from 50 to 70 on ride day.

Nearly all of the route is on Forest Service Roads:  “A ride” nearly all on  Cottonwood Road (1N04) out to just past Reed Creek bridge,  “B ride” adds 3N01 (through Skunk Hollow),  then Cherry Oil Road (1N07) up to Cherry Lake boat ramp, and then west to Reed Creek on 1N04 (Cottonwood, and back to Tuolumne) . Other roads will be Tuolumne County roads (Bay St, Carter St, and Buchanan Road) 

All riders will start between 7:30 and 9 a.m.,  and all will be finished by 4 p.m. 

Support:   there will be three support vehicles with bike racks, water and first aid supplies, as well as three rest and refreshment stops along the way. The main one will be at Reed Creek, and other stops at Cherry Lake Boat Ramp and at the intersection of 1N04 and 3N07. Each stop will have food and water, a 10x10’ pop up canopy , table and chairs.  There is a single unit toilet building at the Boat Ramp, and we plan to have portable toilets located at the other stops.

Traffic and Conduct:   Most of the route is little traveled, except Buchanan Road down to River Ranch; though there may be hunters parked along the route most of the day.  Riders are required to stay to the right as under CVC rules. Helmets are required.   We anticipate no more than 50 riders in this first year, but hope to increase numbers and support in future years.

Organizers:  Velo Promo LLC and the Golden Chain Cyclists. Robert Leibold, the head of both organizations, will be the ride director, and has conducted many recreational rides and road races over the years (since 1972), including the 500-rider Strawberry Fields ride each May in the Watsonville area and the Wards Ferry Road Race in Tuolumne County. Though this event is held under the sanction of USA Cycling, no USA Cycling license is required.

Contacts:  19780 Soulsbyville Road, Soulsbyville, CA  95372; 209 604-1354 velopro1@gmail.com
PresentedBy: Golden Chain Cyclists  and Velo Promo

EventNotes:
THUNDERCROSS CX 

CANCELLED

SUNDAY, OCTOBER 11, 2026

Unfortunately, ThunderCross CX scheduled for October 11 has been canceled due to lower-than-needed registration numbers.

Putting on a quality CX race requires significant upfront commitments for permitting, insurance, officials, timing, and course support. With fewer than 60 racers registered six days out, we can’t responsibly make those commitments while hoping registrations arrive at the last minute.

All registered racers will receive a full refund. No action is required.

We’re incredibly disappointed and sincerely appreciate everyone who registered early and supported the event.

Questions? Contact dennis@rvaracing.com.

Follow @rva_racing and rvaracing.com for what’s next.

Thank you for supporting grassroots racing and RVA Racing.

 

===========================

Race it. Heckle it. Volunteer at it. Bring the family. Bring your friends.

Just don’t hear about how much fun everyone had afterward and wish you’d been there.

Get registered. Get stoked. We’ll see you on the line … or behind the tape.

 

USA CYCLING LICENSES

  • THUNDERCROSS CX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned event.
  • Racers must have a valid USA Cycling license or purchase an eligible one-day license.
  • One-day licenses will be available for racers who need one.

 

85 RACERS. LET’S DO THIS.

Putting on a CX race takes permits, insurance, officials and a whole bunch of behind-the-scenes stuff.

  • We need 85 paid registrations by Monday, October 5 to make THUNDERCROSS happen. If we don’t hit 85, we’ll have to cancel and everyone registered will receive a full refund.

  • Planning to race? Register early. It helps make sure we all get to race.

  • 85 is the magic number. Let’s get there.

 

RACING MORE THAN ONCE?

We like your style.

  • Add additional race categories for just $10 each when you register.

  • Simply select every event you want to race during registration and BikeReg will automatically apply the discount.

More racing. More heckling. More opportunities to tell everyone that this was definitely your “B race.”


BRINGING A PIT BIKE?

Fancy.

  • An additional bib plate for your pit bike is $5. Just select the pit-bike option when you register.

Because nothing says cyclocross like bringing another bicycle specifically for when the first bicycle becomes too muddy.


RACER CHECK-IN

  • Racer check-in opens at 8:00 AM.

  • Check-in for each race closes 30 minutes before that race starts, so give yourself time to get checked in, pin your number, inspect the course, warm up, and contemplate your tire-pressure decisions.

 

NO WALK-UPS. YES. REALLY.

Registration stays open until 6:00 PM the day before the race, so you’ve got plenty of time to make the excellent decision to race THUNDERCROSS.

  • All race additions and category changes must also be completed through BikeReg before registration closes.

  • “But what if I’m not 100% sure I can make it?”

  • We hear you, cupcake.

  • That’s why we’ve got a no-risk registration policy.

  • So register. Put it on the calendar. Start practicing your remounts.

  • Seriously. You can do this.


VACX CHAMPS - YOU EARNED IT

Were you a 2025 VACX Champion? Your championship perks are still good here.

  • USE CODE 26VACXCHAMP to get your $10 entry.

Then make sure you use your code BEFORE registration closes. Don’t leave those hard-earned champ perks sitting on the sidelines.


LET’S GO!

Whether you’re gunning for the podium or just out to support, we can’t wait to see you for an epic day of cyclocross action.

Every race you add on top of your first one of the day is only $10! Do two or three!

This is one of the best courses around! Get ready for lots of ups and downs. It's very spectator friendly as 80% of the course can be seen from the start and finish due to the layout.

Build your skills. Gain confidence. Take it to the trail.

It’s also a great fit for more experienced riders who want to get back to the fundamentals, refine their technique, and develop more efficient movement and bike handling.

No pressure to keep up. No expectation to “just send it.” This is a space to learn, practice, ask questions, make mistakes, and progress at your own pace alongside other women.

October 11 | 10:00 AM–1:00 PM

• Bike handling and skill progression

The focus will be on understanding how and why these techniques work, with plenty of time to practice in a controlled environment before taking them to the trail.

October 25 | 10:00 AM–1:00 PM

EventName: New England Randonneurs 2026 Membership / Season Pass
EventNotes:
This is for 2026 membership and Season Passes in the New England Randonneurs, Inc (NER) organization.

Note: NER membership is NOT the membership required to participate in our events.  Membership in our parent sanctioning body, Randonneurs USA (RUSA) is what is required for events.  However, for the low price of $10, members get NER swag (when available), can participate in NER elections, and help keep randonneuring alive in New England.

Season Pass holders get free admission to all events up to a 400k distance, and a $50 discount on  600k and longer events (including the 1000k/1200k). Online registration & a RUSA Membership is required for free events.  

Details on NER Membership and our events can be found on the NER Website.

Information on registering for RUSA membership can be found on the RUSA Website.

If you volunteered for an event in 2025, you are eligible for FREE 2026 membership and season pass!  If you volunteered in 2025 and did not receive a coupon code, please contact NER volunteer coordinator Emily O'Brien before registering below. 

Hardship Waiver: If you'd like to participate in NER events but circumstances prevent you from being able to afford the membership or entry fees, please email rba@nerandonneurs.org to ask about alternative options. NER is a non-profit, all volunteer organization. Membership & event fees cover expenses.

Gravel Revival 2026

October 16-18, 2026
Peaceful Hills Retreat & Campground • Centerville, TN

Ride Middle TN's finest gravel, camp under the October stars and experience the community that has made Gravel Revival one of the Southeast's favorite grassroots cycling weekends.

Join us for the 7th Annual Gravel Revival—a grassroots gravel festival featuring epic riding, camping, live music, food trucks, beverages, family-friendly activities, and a legendary Saturday night bonfire.

This year's event is intentionally returning to its roots with a participant cap of just 400 riders to preserve the laid-back, community-focused atmosphere that makes Gravel Revival special.

Ride Options

  • 11 Mile Ride
  • 30 Mile Ride
  • 47 Mile Ride/Race
  • 68 Mile Ride/Race

Routes showcase the best of Hickman County gravel, including scenic backroads, fast descents, creek crossings, rugged terrain, and challenging climbs. Final routes will be announced closer to the event.

*New for 2026

The 68-Mile Race will feature our largest cash purse yet:

Overall Men & Women

  • 1st Place: $1,000
  • 2nd Place: $500
  • 3rd Place: $250

Registration Includes

  • Fully supported gravel routes and aid stations
  • Friday evening Shakeout Ride
  • Revival swag kit
  • Access to shower trailer
  • Post-ride meal
  • Complimentary beer, kombucha, and non-alcoholic beverages
  • Live music and Saturday night bonfire
  • Games, prizes, and sponsor giveaways
  • Sunday recovery ride to a local winery and waterfall, including complimentary wine tasting
  • Access to camping and lodging options throughout the weekend

Family-Friendly Fun

Gravel Revival is fun for the entire family - more to come! 

Trail Running Update

Supported trail run routes will not be offered in 2026 due to low participation in recent years. Trail runners are still welcome to camp and enjoy the trails on their own.

Camping & Lodging

Tent camping, RV camping, cabins, cottages, and glamping options are available. Visit our website for complete lodging details and reservations.

Important Notes

  • Registration is limited to 400 participants.
  • This event is self-navigated; GPS devices are strongly recommended.
  • No refunds after August 16, 2026.

For complete event details, lodging information, route updates, FAQs, and sponsor information, visit www.gravelrevival.com.

TREE HOUSE CX

Clinic and Pre-Ride | Friday, October 16th

 River Valley CX Series  | Saturday, October 17th

New England Regional CX Championships | Sunday, October 18th

RAIN OR SHINE EVENT

Tree House Brewing Company | 1 Community Place, South Deerfield, MA 

 

EVENT OVERVIEW

We’re excited to bring you two full days of top-tier NECX racing! Each day offers something different, so be sure to check the details below. Saturday hosts the River Valley CX Series, and Sunday is the New England Regional Cyclocross Championships.

Our mission: deliver a best-in-class New England cyclocross race that ignites the NECX community and thrills Tree House fans alike.  We aim to:

  • Deliver a premium event worthy of the Tree House name
  • Create a race that’s welcoming to all—no matter your sex, ability, or background
  • Give every racer, from first-timers and juniors to seasoned pros, an unforgettable experience
  • Hook new spectators on the thrill of CX

INCLUSIVITY POLICY

Tree House CX is committed to creating a race environment that is safe, welcoming, and inclusive for everyone, regardless of sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, race, religion, disability, or ethnic origin.

We strive to make every participant—from pros to first-time racers, staff to spectators—feel like they belong here. Bullying, harassment, or discriminatory behavior of any kind will not be tolerated. Anyone engaging in such behavior will be asked to leave.

If at any point you feel uncomfortable, unsafe, or witness behavior that makes someone else uncomfortable, please speak to an official or staff member immediately.

WEEKEND SCHEDULE

FRIDAY – Kick off Tree House CX weekend with a full afternoon of fun:

  • Intro to Cyclocross Clinic – 2:45 PM start
  • Open Pre-Ride / Course review

Intro to Cyclocross Clinic - $15
Open to all new and beginner riders, this clinic is your chance to:

  • Ride the actual race course
  • Learn how to navigate twists, turns, and obstacles
  • Build basic skills to boost your confidence on race day
  • Includes free entry to Saturday and/or Sunday race

Clinic & Relay Registration:  Sign up on the registration page.


SATURDAY - River Valley CX Series 

We are excited to once again be part of the River Valley CX Series! 

  • Blunt Park          8/30
  • Hydra Cross       9/5
  • Kilowatt Cross    9/26
  • THCX                   10/17
  • West Hill CX        11/7

 

SUNDAY – 2026 New England Regional Cyclocross Championships

Tree House CX is proud to host the 2026 New England Regional Cyclocross Championships! Podium awards will be presented to the top three finishers in each championship category. Categories Include:

  • Men & Women Elite
  • Men & Women Elite U23
  • Men & Women Junior U13, U15, U17, U19
  • Men Masters 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60-64, 65-69, 70+
  • Women Masters 40-44, 45-49, 50-54, 55-59, 60+, 70+
  • Non-Binary Open

Eligibility: To be eligible for a championship podium, riders must:

  • Hold an active USA Cycling annual license
  • Reside in the New England Region

Full NEBRA guidelines and eligibility details: nebra.us/nebra-state-and-regional-championship-event-guidelines
 

REGISTRATION

  • Pre-Registration closes Thursday, October 15th at 5:00 PM ET
  • Late Registration opens on BikeReg at 9:00 AM Friday, October 16th.
    • Expect limited spots due to sold-out fields in past years
    • Prices increase by $10 starting October 16th
    • Late registrants are staged at the back of the field
  • Early bib pick-up: Friday, October 16th from 1:00–5:00 PM
  • Day-of bib pick-up: Opens at 7:30 AM on Saturday & Sunday
  • Additional same-day races: $20 each
  • Race field limits are posted in the race schedule


COURSE PRE RIDE

  • Course preview is open between 12 PM - 6:00 PM on Friday, October 16th.
  • Course pre-ride opens at 7:00 am on Saturday and Sunday.
  • You may warm-up and ride the course in between races.
  • Absolutely no pre-riding during a race.If you are riding the course between races, you must ride behind, and not pass, the last rider in the race.


FIRST-TIME RACERS
New to cyclocross? We’ve got you. Join our Intro to Cyclocross Clinic on Friday, October 16th, where you’ll ride the actual course, learn how to tackle turns and obstacles, and pick up skills to boost your confidence for race day. Mountain, gravel, fat, or commuter bikes with tires 35mm+ are perfect. Sign up right on the registration page, and email B2C2Cycling@gmail.com with any questions. We can’t wait to cheer you on!


STAGING & STARTING ORDER

Saturday (River Valley CX Series): The first row will be staged by River Valley CX Series points, followed by CrossResults Points. Riders who register after October 16th will be staged at the back of the field as part of the last call-up.

Sunday (New England Regional CX Championships): Races will be staged by CrossResults Points. Riders who register after October 16th will be staged at the back of the field as part of the last call-up.


LAPPED RIDERS
While the final decision rests with USA Cycling Officials, we have not pulled lapped riders in past years and do not expect to do so this year.


KIDS FUN RACE
A special race just for the little ones! All bikes are welcome—balance bikes, BMX, mountain, gravel, you name it. Kids will ride a dedicated lap on a safe, kid-friendly portion of the actual course. Join us at 1:15 on both days, under the Finish Arch! Event is FREE, but all parents/guardians MUST sign the USA Cycling waiver via online registration or at on-site registration.


FOOD & BEVERAGES

  • We’re excited to keep you fueled and refreshed all weekend with:
  • Tree House Beverages – Pouring begins at 11:00 AM
  • Tree House Pizza – Fresh slices starting at Noon (slices only on race day)
  • Tree House Coffee Cart – Hot & cold coffee available all day
  • Outside Food Vendors  
    • Thai Chili Truck - Friday, Saturday, Sunday
    • Crazy Arepas - Saturday
    • Soulfully Vegan - Sunday
    • Wake the Dead Donuts - Sunday

Note: Outside alcohol is not permitted on the property.

PARKING

Event parking will be located in the Northernmost area of the Tree House property. It will be on a grass soccer field North of the paved lot. The race course will be on the South side of the property, it is about a ¼ mile away, so plan accordingly


TEAM TENTS

We’re once again hosting team tents in the South Field—right along the start line. Space is limited to 40 spots. Each reservation includes:

  • Space for one 10x10 tent
  • Parking for one car or van

Need more room? Simply purchase additional spots.


LODGING

There are a lot of college weekends in the area, so lodging is limited. Here are a few options available as of September 15th. On-site camping is NOT permitted.

  • Red Roof Inn - West Springfield - 30 min drive
    https://www.redroof.com/property/ma/west-springfield/rri193
     
  • Berkshire East Camping - Charlemont, MA about 35 minutes
    https://berkshireeast.com/summer/camping
     
  • White Birch Campground - Whately about 2 miles from Tree House
    https://whitebirchcampmass.com/

PETS

Well-behaved, on-leash dogs are welcome on brewery grounds, outside of the building. Please have them say hi to event staff!

EventNotes:
There will be Satellite Locations to ride and participate in the 11th Annual TDM Bike Ride. One Satellite Location will be in Northern Virginia at the Caboose Brewery (520 Mill Street Vienna, VA 22180). The second Satellite Location will be at the Dismal Swamp Canal Trail and Big Ugly Brewery in Chesapeake, VA. Satellite locations will be connected virtually to the Main Ride location at the Midnight Brewery. Riders at Satellite locations will ride, run, or walk their own distances along bike paths in the area of the breweries and return to the designated Satellite location no later than noon on event day to be part of the after-ride event. The Dismal Swam Canal Trail location will also offer a 50K Ride through the Chesapeake countryside. Riders at the satellite location will receive an event glass (all participants will receive two brewery vouchers to be used on event day for brewery products not to exceed a specified amount). They will also receive any merchandise or raffle tickets they purchased online. Raffle tickets may or may not be sold on event day at the satellite locations as the tickets will be drawn at the Midnight Brewery on Event Day. 

This will be the 11th Annual Tour de Midnight at the Main location which is a bike ride event starting from and returning to the Midnight Brewery located at 2410 Granite Ridge Road in Rockville, VA 23146. This event supports the Epilepsy Foundation of Virginia (all proceeds go to EFVA and 97% of these funds stay in Virginia to support Virginians).  Come and see the beauty of the fall foliage as we traverse through Central Virginia.  We will briefly head north on Ashland Road before taking a left turn on VA-271 Pouncey Tract Road.  60-70 Mile riders will see the farms of Rockville, the historic town of Montpelier, breathtaking views like the Woodson Mill and capture stunning views of Lake Anna. Our 33 Mile riders will enjoy Montpelier and Rockville's breathtaking country settings. The 17 Mile route will take riders through Rockville and the Dunn's Chapel area that provides a great ride through the countryside. 

At the Main Ride Location: Participants will be invited to enjoy the hospitality of Midnight Brewery after their ride.  Enjoy live music, fun zone, paint your pumpkin purple contest, and a custom pint glass that all participants receive (all participants will receive two brewery vouchers to be used on event day for brewery products not to exceed a specified amount). There will be food trucks for everyone to enjoy.  There will be police support at the major intersections. EventName: The Breakaway Gravel Race at Echo Cliff
EventNotes:
The Breakaway
Presented by Ad Astra Bike Co.
Saturday, October 17th – 9:30 AM | Echo Cliff Park, Maple Hill, KS (Close to Dover, KS)
Break Away. Ride Hard. Find Your Freedom.

Join us for The Breakaway — a gritty gravel race through the Flint Hills, starting and finishing at the iconic Echo Cliff Park in Maple Hill, Kansas. Go the extra mile on some fantastic gravel, push through the dust, and discover what it takes to break free from the ordinary.

Routes & Elevation - View and Download Routes Here!

The Sprint – 13 Miles | 958 ft Elevation
Short, fast, and perfect for those who want to test their legs without going all in. Perfect for beginner riders looking to build their confidence! A quick loop packed with scenic gravel, rolling hills, and just enough challenge to make you earn it. Ideal for new riders or anyone looking to hammer from start to finish. This is an out 6.5 mile and back 6.5 route. Same route as last year.
 

The Quick Break – 25 Miles | 1,548 ft Elevation
A fast and fierce route for riders ready to taste the challenge. Rolling gravel, wide horizons, and a SAG + First Aid Station to keep you fueled and flying.
 

The Breakout – 46 Miles | 2,716 ft Elevation
Longer, more challenging, and made for those who crave the grind. Featuring climbs that’ll demand it all from you. Includes a SAG + First Aid Stations to keep you rolling strong.
 

The Full Breakaway – 72 Miles | 4,173 ft Elevation
The XL takes you farther into the Flint Hills, where long gravel stretches, and sustained climbs define the day. Designed for riders who appreciate the grind as much as the views, this route delivers a full-bodied gravel experience with SAG and First Aid Stations supporting you throughout.

Event Details
• Date: Saturday, October 17th
• Start Time: 9:30 AM
• Location: Echo Cliff Park, Maple Hill, KS
• Support: SAG and First Aid coverage on all routes
• Raffle: Every Rider will receive 1 raffle ticket for some awesome prizes!
• Requirements: Helmets & Water bottle required | Gravel-ready bikes recommended

Why You’ll Love It
• Classic Flint Hills gravel and unforgettable views
• Three challenging routes to push your limits
• Grit, grind, and friendly competition
• Post-ride community and camaraderie
• The Breakout — where riders earn freedom through effort

To participate, racers will compete in the first day of racing on 10/17 at the 2026 Syracuse Cyclocross GP in Liverpool, NY and the second day of racing on 10/18 at Marbletown Madness CX in Newark, NY. Points will be awarded to every racer competing as follows:

Licensing Requirements:   This is a USA Cycling sanctioned event. All riders must present a valid license at registration and sign an event release form (minors must have a parent/guardian sign).  One-day and annual licenses will be available for purchase at registration. Current USAC Fee Schedule here. https://usacycling.org/memberships-old/one-day-licenses
PA STATE CHAMPIONSHIP INFO: Only USA Cycling Annual License Holders from PA are eligible for the championship title.

Call-up Protocol:  Call ups will be given based on PA Cyclocross Series Standings and rules. Above all we will use promoters discretion. If you yell at the promoter you will go to the back. 

Lapped Riders:  Lapped riders will finish on the same lap as the leaders.  Riders in danger of being lapped must yield to oncoming racers and are not to interfere with their progress or trail behind them. Laps are pretty fast on this course, and come in around 7-8 minutes. We'll try not to pull riders if we don't have to.

Results:  Results will be posted at the registration area.  Results will be made final 15 minutes after being posted.  The top 3 finishers in every event must report immediately to the start/finish line for awards and photos.

Inclusivity Statement: We really only have one rule on Ciclismo, and it's “don't be a jerk”. Nobody remembers whether you won some race or not, but they will remember forever if you were not nice to them. In the effort to make cyclocross an inclusive space for new and seasoned participants, we welcome all to join us at our events, and will not tolerate hate (actual hate, not to be confused with haterz) disrespect, bigotry, racism, transphobia, or anything else that has no place in modern society, let alone a grassroots bike race. Should you have an issue with any of these on race day, we have your back.

EventName: Mountain Biking Skills Clinic Pleasant Grove Park
EventNotes:
Are you looking for a local mountain biking skills Clinic to learn more about trail riding?  You found it!  If you would like to take your riding to the next level, this is where you belong.  You will learn and practice basic mountain biking skills necessary to navigate the trail system at Pleasant Grove Park.  The skills covered include body position, bike separation, shifting, braking, climbing, descending, and dealing with minor obstacles.  We will also talk about trail user communication and trail etiquette.

You are welcome to bring your own trail ready bike, or we can provide bikes and helmets at no cost.  Inventory is limited so get one soon!  Schedule a tune up or a bike fitting by calling Matthew at 434-987-9379 or email mstancil@fluvanna.gov.

The Dutch Hall Enduro is a FREE gravel race with the option to race 30-60-90 miles all within the same 30 mile loop, no HWY crossings. Starting at Arkfeld Acres, check-in will start at 7am. We will all take off together at 8am on a neutral roll out from the farm until we hit N 192nd St. Your race will start from there taking you through the small Village of Washington just north of Dutch Hall Rd. The small park in Washington will be your aid station and the start of a new 30 mile loop. Each distance will have a slightly diff. color on your race plate to help with managing who's who on course. Once you've completed your 1, 2, or 3 loop's through Washington head back to the farm carefully navigating your way to the finish line. At the finish we will have food and refreshments provided by Arkfeld Acres and MGrills. Official timing will be through Race Results and we will have podium payouts for top 5 in the 90 and top 3 in 60/30 both male/female.

Total prize purse will be $5,000.

Thank you to our sponsors for their support and generosity!

Arkfeld Acres, Arkfeld Wealth Strategies, Dvorak Law, MGrills, Kinney MFG, Goodlife Nutrition, Foothill Products.

Special Thanks to Andy and Kama Arkfeld for their continued support throughout the cycling community and making this happen. This is going to be a great fall day for racing gravel in Nebraska!!

Registration IS OPEN! 

Starting point will be Odell at the City Park on Main Street. We will be doing things little different this year and doing a series of Loops to add up to 70 miles. You can pick how many loops you want to do, anything from 23 miles, 47 miles or all three for 70 miles. Yes, we have copied what Haddam Hounds did this year and see how it works for us.   There will be one SAG stop located at the City Park and the option of also heading over the Odell grocery store for some food options there as well. 
 
This will be a no drop ride, we will regroup every 10 miles or so. 
 
 The route will NOT be marked so you will have to be able to download them!
 
There will be pie afterwards!

EventNotes:
Bike touring is the best! While we would love to drop everything and head out on our bikes for weeks at a time, life gets in the way and so, welcome to Sub-24 Hour bike camping.

Each summer, in spring and fall, we host these overnight camping trips to spots in Pinckney, Brighton and beyond. The goal is to get out there and back in under 24 hours and sprinkle in a little adventure into our local lives. So pack your bikes, leave room for some firewood and join us for our next trip.

What unfolds on these trips is a mini celebration of all the things we love about bikes. Good friends & new friends. A casual pace with stops for snacks and pictures. Racks overburdened by firewood. And a night spent around the campfire catching up and dreaming about the season ahead, or behind.

We have reserved the entire campground at Blind Lake once again and there will be plenty of space for all!

UTCX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned series and follows USA Cycling’s Competition Category Policy.

is it a party? a challenge? an adventure?….

that's up to YOU…. but we can promise a proper tour of knoxville's awesome Urban Wilderness (a.k.a. dirty south) and beyond, and a party with bike friends into the night!  to be clear, this isn't some fancy marked race course with lots of aid stations… you are on your own to be self-sufficient and be prepared (just like any group/solo ride you might do).  you will get info on available water stops, convenience stores, and there's a really good chance you'll find some “trail magic” in a few places.  routes will be provided via gpx, and we will have maps to help with the tricky spots.

the ScruffyCat was born out of the idea of a riding ALL the knoxville trails in one huge route, and just so happens it's right around 100mi.  from new trail to old goat-paths, we linked all the goods with the best road connections through and around town.  but be warned… just because it's not in the big mountains or forest-lands, doesn't mean it doesn't make for a big ole day on the bike!

if you're looking for more of “sampler”, consider the ScrappyKitty for an awesome chunk of trails without being quite a far-reaching and wild.  just like SC100, it offers a good variety of trail and links good roads the way us locals do all the time.

not so sure about a biting off either of the bigger two routes?  come check out the SuperKitten!  it's a chance for a tour of all of the “dirty south” highlights.. created to offer a shorter day but a great time for younger cats (or perhaps the most-sensible sorts).

regardless of what route you choose, the day is all about seeing what knoxville has to offer, and sharing it with friends, near and far!  come and ride, then stay and party… we will have a solid offering of snacks, drinks, and home-cooked goods to fuel you back up for the bonfire.

and if saturday is not enough, we will also do a social hair of the cat ride on sunday!  it's a great chance to see the only area of trails in knoxville that the SC100 doesn't hit.

all the deets and specifics will be shared via email to those who register, and please register soon! **we need a headcount to provide all the eats and good times for you**

we had such a ball sending last year's crew home with some custom wearables, that we're planning to screen-print again.  just bring whatever you want tagged with this year's SW-designed artwork… we don't promise it'll be purfect, but it will be rad!  [details to follow in confirmation email or carrier-pigeon]

LOCATION AVAILABLE ONCE YOU REGISTER!

 

Registration/Check in: Registration/check in will start at 8:00am on Saturday, October 17th and at 8:30am on Sunday, October 18th.

 

Parking: There is plenty of parking off the fire roads and near the expo once you enter the gate. There will be an $8 one-time entrance fee, payable via CASH ONLY (cell service is spotty to non-existent so venmo won’t be an option - unless you pay ahead of time to @Sam-Ayers-1 on venmo. Include your name and/or license plate number). Please park in the designated pull-outs or parking lot.

 

Accommodations: There will be no onsite camping at the Ranch, however there are plenty of great camping and other lodging options nearby. Scotts Flat Campground is a great go-to camp spot not far up Highway 20 from the venue. Inn Town Campground is a nice glamping option right in Nevada City. Gold Miner's Inn in Grass Valley is a nice hotel option. There are also lots of Airbnb’s and Vrbo’s in the area.

 

A word on the property: Massive shoutout and unlimited thanks to Ron Sanchez and the Sanchez family for permitting us to utilize this beautiful land for our collegiate race! We are beyond blessed to be able to use this special property, but there are a few things we all gotta do if we want to potentially race here again! First and foremost: THIS IS PRIVATE PROPERTY! This is not an East Bay Regional Park, this is not national forest, this isn’t even Highway 9 loamers. This is PRIVATE! You aren’t allowed to ride here before or after the race. You can follow @tds_enduro on Instagram to find work days; dig enough dirt and you may be allowed to ride here. Otherwise: stay away! That is part of what makes this event such a privilege. On a related note: do not ride trails that are not in any of the 5 races! Seriously! Anyone caught poaching will be promptly run out of town. We’re racing sick trails already…stick to them! It’s just a safety thing. Additionally: NO STRAVA! We cannot afford to let heatmaps blow this place up. Again: it’s just a safety thing. You’re welcome to record your rides but PLEASE make them private!!! Like any place you’re a guest at: be respectful. Don’t destroy things. Don’t light things on fire. Don’t be dumb. It’s not hard. Osborne Hill Road is a small road with numerous residents on it: drive cautiously please!!! Other than that, have a fun time, enjoy yourself, and ride your bike!

 

Pre-ride: Friday pre-ride will start at 12pm, and will close at 4:00pm. Please stick to the designated RACE COURSES ONLY. All other trails are off limits. All courses will be open for pre-ride on Saturday and Sunday as well. Note: the SuperD and Downhill courses will cross near the top, so pay attention to cross traffic when pre-riding.

 

Medical: For Friday’s pre-ride, we will not have medical assistance on-site, but if something needs attention, please refer to the number and address below! Bouchier Pritchett Family Medicine will be on standby to address any ailments that may arise. Try to contact the race director Sam Ayers (206) 734-9799 or Justin Peck (203) 448-8268before making the mission. On Saturday and Sunday there will be medical assistance available on-site at the general expo/staging area! Look for someone in a red shirt with a white cross if you need help, healing, or just some company. Give them a big thank you if you see them, they’re just volunteers here to help!

 

Jon Pritchett (530) 470-3253

Bouchier Pritchett Family Medicine 280 Sierra College Dr #207, Grass Valley, CA 95945

 

Podiums: Podiums will take place at the end of each day in the expo area once all racers and officials have returned from the trails and the results are finalized. If you cannot stay until the end of the day and made top 3, let us know so we can get you your prize before you head out.

RICHMOND FESTIVAL OF CROSS IS HERE!

CHIMBORAZO CX

SATURDAY, OCTOBER 17, 2026

ONE WEEKEND. A WHOLE LOT OF CROSS.

Chimborazo CX isn't just another bike race - It's Richmond in October. 

Yup - Chimborazo CX is back.

Race it. Heckle it. Volunteer at it. Bring the family. Bring your friends.

Just don’t hear about how much fun everyone had afterward and wish you’d been there.

Get registered. Get stoked. We’ll see you on the line … or behind the tape.

 

85 RACERS. LET’S DO THIS.

Putting on a CX race takes permits, insurance, officials and a whole bunch of behind-the-scenes stuff.

  • We need 85 PAID registrations by Monday, October 12 to make CHIMBORAZO CX happen. If we don’t hit 85, we’ll have to cancel and everyone registered will receive a full refund.

  • Planning to race? Register early. It helps make sure we all get to race.

  • 85 is the magic number. Let’s get there.


USA CYCLING LICENSES

  • CHIMBORAZO CX is a USA Cycling-sanctioned event.
  • Racers must have a valid USA Cycling license or purchase an eligible one-day license.
  • One-day licenses will be available for racers who need one.

 

RACING MORE THAN ONCE?

We like your style.

  • Add additional race categories for just $10 each when you register.

  • Simply select every event you want to race during registration and BikeReg will automatically apply the discount.

More racing. More heckling. More opportunities to tell everyone that this was definitely your “B race.”


BRINGING A PIT BIKE?

Fancy.

  • An additional bib plate for your pit bike is $5. Just select the pit-bike option when you register.

  • Because nothing says cyclocross like bringing another bicycle specifically for when the first bicycle becomes too muddy.


RACER CHECK-IN

  • Racer check-in opens at 8:00 AM.

  • Check-in for each race closes 30 minutes before that race starts, so give yourself time to get checked in, pin your number, inspect the course, warm up, and contemplate your tire-pressure decisions.

 

NO WALK-UPS. YES. REALLY.

Registration stays open until 6:00 PM the day before the race, so you’ve got plenty of time to make the excellent decision to race CHMBORAZO CX.

  • All race additions and category changes must also be completed through BikeReg before registration closes.

  • “But what if I’m not 100% sure I can make it?”

  • We hear you, cupcake.

  • That’s why we’ve got a no-risk registration policy.

  • So register. Put it on the calendar. Start practicing your remounts.

  • Seriously. You can do this.


VACX CHAMPS - YOU EARNED IT

Were you a 2025 VACX Champion? Your championship perks are still good here - even though Chimborazo CX is not this year’s VACX Championship race.

  • USE CODE 26VACXCHAMP to get your $10 entry.

Then make sure you use your code BEFORE registration closes. Don’t leave those hard-earned champ perks sitting on the sidelines.


LET’S GO!

Whether you’re gunning for the podium or just out to support, we can’t wait to see you for an epic day of cyclocross action.

EventNotes:
Welcome to the 2026 NOMBS Series Finale at The Thorn MTB Trail!

THIS EVENT IS RAIN OR SHINE!

Day Of Registration:

While we strongly encourage you to preregister (and greatly appreciate you doing so as it helps the event go more smoothly), there will be "day of" registration. It will be an extra $10 after 6pm Saturday evening, and will close 60 minutes before the start of your event.

Race day Schedule:

  • 9am plate pickup opens
  • 9:30am Cat 3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race day of registration closes
  • 10am Cat3 Jr Novice U19-U13 & Kids race start
  • 11:30 am plater pickup closes.
  • 11:40 am Jr Novice podiums and riders Meeting
  • 12pm Cat 1 categories start
  • 12:40pm All remaining cat 2 and cat 3 categories start. THIS TIME IS APPROXIMATE!
  • 2:30-3pm, all podiums.
  • Adaptive racers, we may alter where in the schedule you start as we work with you and learn what works best. 

!!!!!!!Start time notes!!!!!

In an effort to offer a safer and more fun race environment for all participants we are now starting Cat 2 and Cat 3 racers after Cat 1 and E Bikes have completed one lap. This greatly reduces conflict between very fast cat 1 and E Bike racers passing novice racers by nearly eliminating lap traffic. The posted start time of 12:40m for cat 2 & 3 is approximate. We will begin releasing the remaining cat 2 & 3 waves after Cat 1 racers go through scoring. Know your wave number!

10am Cat3 Jr. Novice Races

You may have noticed that we are doing Cat3 Jr novice races early in the day and be asking "hey, what's up with that?" We want to give Jr's, and particularly novice Jr's the best race day experience we can. Separating the Jr. novice races to an earlier start allows us to do 3 things:

  • Fewer racers on course for the race.
  • For families where the one or both parents also race it gives the parents a chance to spectate and cheer their kids.
  • Novice Jr's get their own start, with more people cheering and spectating. Bring the cowbells!

USA Cycling Licenses, and NOMBS Series Championship rules & eligibility:

NOMBS is proud to be bringing a USAC sanctioned series to Ohio and be hosting the official USA Cycling Ohio MTB Championship. Partnering with USA Cycling helps us offer you a great series with structure, consistent categories & scoring, good insurance for landowners, and allows an opportunity for riders with goals outside Ohio to earn USAC points. 

USA Cycling Race Age:

 Your “race age” is the age you will be on December 31st. This rule exists so that a person does not have to change the age group they are entering partway through a race season. 

NOMBS Series Championship Eligibility rules:

  1. A rider must have a current USA Cycling License (need not reside in Ohio).
  2. Must race in the season finale race.
  3. Scored on best 5 races.
  4. In the event of a points tie the season final race is the tie breaker.

Part of the exciting Roanoke GO Fest (Go Outside Festival), this cross-country mountain bike race brings high-energy racing to one of Virginia’s premier trail systems. Check out the rules for Go Nuts Series!
1) You must complete race on the bike you started on.  
2) Must wear bike helmet and appropriate gear.
3) Must follow outlined trail, any shortcuts or variations will result in disqualification.
4) You must make any and all mechanical repairs yourself or utilize the local bike support (if available).
6) You can move up in a Category, but never down.
7) Good sportsmanship is a MUST, any bad behavior will result in disqualification.
8) Please use proper trail etiquette during course recon and transfer stages.
9) All protest must be filed within 20 minutes of the last competitor completing the final race stage of the day. 
10) If you encounter an injured/downed rider, please stop and check on them. If a rider is seriously injured or unconscious, let officials know immediately or call 911.
 

Go Nuts (GNR) eMTB Rules as follows: 
1) Maximum 750watts - assistance up to 20 miles per hour - Pedaling assistance only. No hand or foot throttle allowed. Automatic disqualification. Bicycles must remain locked, i.e., no modification of wheel sensor from factory circumference or any other modification to manipulate the factory set speed of the bike.
2) Throttle mechanisms are prohibited.
3) Studded tires are prohibited.
4) It is forbidden to change e-bike during the event even if the rider finishes the event with the same race plate.
5) It is forbidden to recharge the e-bike or battery in the technical zone during the GNR event.
6) Technical assistance consists of the replacement or repairs of any part of the e-bike at the exception of the frame, wheels or battery.
7) Riders age categories are 18 and under, 19-39, 40-49 and 50 plus for Classes; Amateurs, Experts and Open Pro. 
8) Riders can only use the battery in place on their bike and cannot carry or switch out an additional battery during the competition.
9) eMTB is not a USA Cycling category as of now,  so points are not awarded nationally. USAC license is not required.
10) Race course length will be 4.5 - 7 miles depending on difficulty. Steeper climbs and more technical than normal XC will be tested on some courses. Each category will start an hour apart and should be completed within their hour.
11) Races will be conducted regardless of weather conditions.  In the event of rain or other unfavorable conditions, it may be necessary to alter the order of the event schedule, including but not limited to, adjusting the length of the race or delaying or stopping the program completely.  Should a delay occur, every effort will be made to resume the schedule in a timely fashion if conditions significantly improve.
12) No headphones, earphones or sound devices permitted. Horns and bells are permitted.
13) Riders are required to wear the appropriate helmet. Other protective gear is optional; gloves, goggles, elbow/knee guards, etc.
14) Shirt, shoes, and pants/shorts required. Clipless or flat pedals are both permitted.
15) An E-Mountain Bike is a bike operated with two energy sources, human pedal power and an electric engine, which only provides assistance when the rider is pedaling.
16) The course will the taped and marked. Any rider cutting the course will be disqualified.
17) Any behavior deemed in appropriate or unsportsmanlike like conduct will not be tolerated. Verbal or physical infractions will result in a disqualification.

Severe weather policy
Unless otherwise posted, race will be held. Safety of all racers is our main priority. If there is a delay or cancellation due to weather conditions, racers are responsible for checking information posted by director.
The information will be posted on the homepage of website, social network avenues, and via email up to 72 hours prior to the race.

Transfer/Refund Policy
There will be no registration refunds once registration is processed. We will allow transfers to upcoming races. All transfers must be requested 10 days prior and is only allowed for races that were rescheduled. Transfers will not be allowed 10 days before race or after race.

E-BIKE REGULATIONS (THIS IS A WORK IN PROGRESS....LEARNING AS WE GO....)
As we continue to provide e-bike racing in the Month of Mud series we want it to be a safe but welcoming racing environment for all mountain bike enthusiasts and racers. In order to do so we believe the following standards are fair for our local grassroots series.
• E- Bikes that are USAC UCI or GNCC certified are legal.
• E-Bikes must pedal assist with a max speed of 20mph.
• Programmable E-Bikes must be set and locked to 750 watts and 20 MPH. • Throttle mechanisms are prohibited. • Boost buttons must be removed or disabled. • No aftermarket modifications will be allowed.
• E-Bikes must be inspected 30 minutes before the race start. • E-Bikes MUST be in the off position at the starting line and powered up at the official's instructions. • Settings must be verified immediately after finishing. • Any E-Bike that is found to be illegal, rider will forfeit all prizes and points and will be suspended for remaining races. All categories. • Officials carry the right to test any E-Bike in question. Month of mud is not liable for any damage that may occur during testing. If you withhold your E-Bike to this test, you will be disqualified from the race.
• Passing etiquette must be followed. Unsportsmanlike behavior, foul riding, use of profanity, or flagrant discourtesy directed at participants, spectators, or officials will result in disqualification.
• Analog bikes have the right of way, you must yield to a racer in a different class to pass you when appropriate and safe to do so.
• No battery swapping during the race
 
OTHER NOTES:
· Helmets are required for all races.
· Please arrive early to check in. Check-in closes 30 minutes prior to start times.

EventNotes:
HILL YEAH RIDE

GET IN TOUCH WITH YOUR HYR SELF.

Sunday, October 18, 2026 | 8:00 AM
The Lost Abbey | Vista, California

WHO DOESN’T LOVE ASCENSION?

One last ride. One last rip. One very good reason to refuse to let the season end quietly. After all, Hell No! The season isn’t over until Hill Yeah says it is.

Welcome to the Hill Yeah Ride (HYR), Southern California’s end-of-season celebration of everything we love about riding bikes: pavement and dirt, climbing and descending, suffering and smiling, competition and camaraderie, followed by food, beer, bikes and the glorious retelling of things that may or may not have happened exactly the way you remember them.

This isn’t a gran fondo.
It isn’t a gravel race.
It isn’t a road race.
And it sure as hell isn’t another Sunday coffee ride.

It’s Hill Yeah.

We roll from The Lost Abbey in Vista at 8:00 AM onto a specially concocted course mixing road and unroad, with enough climbing to earn the name and enough surprises to keep everyone entertained.

Want to hammer? Hammer.

Want to chase KOM/QOM glory? There are timed Strava segments waiting for you.

Want to ride hard with your friends, explore some dirt and finish the season with a story worth embellishing over a beer? You have found your people.

And when the riding ends, Hill Yeah keeps rolling.

Back at The Lost Abbey, the parking lot transforms into a cycling bazaar and end-of-season gathering with a bike swap and expo, food trucks, beer garden, cycling brands, gear, bikes, friends and fellow riders.

Buy something.

Sell something.

Eat something.

Drink something.

Talk about bikes with people who are perfectly happy to talk about bikes for an unreasonable amount of time.

RIDE IT. RACE IT. CELEBRATE IT.

Hill Yeah was built around a radical concept:

Cycling should be fun.

So come race the segments. Come ride the unroad. Come hunt for treasure at the bike swap. Come have lunch. Come drink a beer. Come hang out.

Or come do all of it.

$50 gets you into the Hill Yeah Ride, including the ride, event activities and eligibility to contest the KOM/QOM competition.

THE HILL YEAH SUNDAY

6:30 AM | Packet pickup opens
7:30 AM | Rider staging
7:45 AM | Rider briefing
8:00 AM | HILL YEAH! Ride starts
11:00 AM | Beer garden + food trucks open
12:00 PM | Bike swap + expo opens
1:00 PM | KOM/QOM cutoff
2:00 PM | KOM/QOM recognition
6:00 PM | We reluctantly call it a day but we're sure there is an after party

GET IN TOUCH WITH YOUR HYR SELF.

Bring your road bike.
Bring your gravel bike.
Bring whatever bike makes you happy.

Bring your friends. Bring your legs. Bring your appetite.

Ride hard. Get dirty. Go uphill. Come back down. Chase something. Find something. Eat something. Drink something.

And end the season on a HYR note.

HILL YEAH.

ROAD • UNROAD • KOM/QOM • BIKE SWAP • FOOD • BEER • BIKES • GOOD TIMES

Because the season isn’t over until you say it is.

EventNotes:
Back by popular demand!  Come out and enjoy the blazing fall colors at the seventh annual BRANDYWINE VALLEY ROUBAIX FALL FOLIAGE Gravel Grinder. 

This Gravel Grinder / Gran Fondo / Group Ride will take riders through the scenic country-side and rolling hills of the Brandywine Valley, some of the most unspoiled and historic countryside of the Mid-Atlantic.  These paved and gravel roads are even more beautiful in the fall with trees ablaze with fall foliage!  After an amazingly successful first 6 years, the BVR Fall Foliage is back again for 2026.  With cool fall weather and beautiful fall scenery this ride offers the perfect opportunity for one more autumn ride to wind down the 2026 cycling season.  This ride is 53 miles with over 60%+ consisting of gravel / mixed surface roads including several newly added gravel sections just for the special BVR Fall Foliage event.  For the BVRFF addition we will be doubling up certain sections of gravel and this will give portions of the course a whole new feel!!!  The course is suited for gravel, cyclocross, mtn, and road bikes (min 28 mm tires).  Please note, for the BVRFF there will not be an official road bypass option and the Hill Top and Donut Hill climbs are not featured.  However, there will be "world famous" apple cider donuts at the rest stop...the perfect mid ride snack!

This will not be a mass start evert, but rather a staggered start to avoid large crowds of riders.  Start with your group anytime between 9 and 10 AM.  Registration table will be open at 8:30 to answer question and for shirt pick-up.  If you want to get an earlier start, go for it!

Please support our generous sponsors: Piscitello Law, The Whip Tavern, Holly Gross Group,  The Fence Authority, without them, our event is not possible.

Event pricing: $45.00, online registration only.  Limited availability day-of registration $55 cash only.  

As with all previous BVR events a portion of the proceeds will benefit two local charities.  Quest Therapeutics (www.questtherapeutic.com) is an equestrian facility utilizing horse riding to provide therapy for children with physical and developmental challenges.  Our second charity is the Pennsylvania Interscholastic Mountain Bike Association (www.pamtb.org), a grass-roots organization developing high and middle school mountain bike programs in our immediate area.

The BVR Fall Foliage is a self supported ride and all riders are responsible for their own mechanical support.  A feed stop and facilities will be located at approximately mile marker 25.

Hope you can make it out and please spread the word. 

BVR FF Event Directors

Bob, Scott & Shawn

Please support our generous sponsors: Piscitello Law, The Whip Tavern, Holly Gross Group,  The Fence Authority, without them, our event is not possible.

The Brandywine Valley Roubaix Fall Foliage passes through some of the most beautiful scenery in the Mid-Atlantic region, here are some recent pictures along the way...of course the trees you see here will be ablaze with fall foliage colors:

Brookside Cross – Five Mile Creek

Brutally fun on the banks of Five Mile Creek, with a mix of natural features and tough obstacles.

  • Creekside sand: Deep, shifting sand pits by the water.
  • Playground gravel: Pea gravel grind that kills momentum.
  • Steep run-up: Bike on the shoulder, legs on fire.
  • Forested terrain: Fast and flowing through the trees.

Brookside Cross is pure variety — sand, gravel, run-ups, and forest flow, all packed into one brutally fun course.

Never raced?
Perfect. Start here.

First CX race? Adults should choose the appropriate Novice field. Learn more about cyclocross.

First XCC race? Adults should choose the category that best matches their experience. If you're new to MTB racing, start with Novice/Intermediate. Learn more about XCC.

Junior? Choose the appropriate age-group race—but keep reading, because CX and mountain bike racing use different racing ages.

Still not sure? Send us a message through BikeReg. We'd rather help you find the right race than make you decipher the rulebook.

Junior parents
Same kid. Two racing ages. Because bike racing.
Cyclocross
Age on December 31, 2027
XCC / Mountain Bike
Age on December 31, 2026
A rider born in 2018, for example, is CX racing age 9 but mountain-bike racing age 8. That rider may enter CX 9–10, but is still a Youth rider for XCC and should race our U9 Kids Race rather than Junior XCC 9–10.
HELPFUL details
What you need to know before you sign up.
Check-in + registration
Check-in opens at 7:30 AM. Registration and check-in for each race close 15 minutes before its scheduled start.
Team tents
Reserved team-tent space with premium parking is available as a $20 registration add-on.
Call-ups
CX call-ups are based on crossresults.com points; Novice fields line up by registration order. XCC riders will be called up by USA Cycling XC category (Pro, Cat 1, Cat 2, then Cat 3) and by registration order within each category. Riders registering after the early-registration window closes will be called up behind all other riders in their XCC race category.
Neutral race support
Patapsco Bikes will be on site providing neutral race support. 
Race rules + what to expect
Keep it simple. Keep it legal. Keep it fun.
Forney Road area + pre-riding
The new Forney Road parking lot and event area will not open to the public until November. Outside of race day, please do not enter or attempt to pre-ride the race course; construction and event setup may be underway. Bacon Ridge’s existing public trails remain accessible from other trailheads.
Weather
CX and XCC are rain or shine. Course layout may be adjusted if conditions require it.
USA Cycling
USA Cycling rules apply to all sanctioned CX and XCC races. View the current USA Cycling rulebook.
CX equipment
Mountain bikes are allowed! Bar ends are not. Helmets and jerseys with sleeves are mandatory. You can stow an extra bike and receive equipment support in the pit during the race.
XCC equipment
Mountain bikes are strongly encouraged. Rigid bikes if you dare. No e-bikes. Helmets required. There is no tech zone or bike pit for the race. Riders should be prepared to handle their own mechanicals during the race.
Staging
Riders should report to staging 10 minutes before their scheduled start. Do not enter the course while a race is underway.
Prizes
Cash purse for Men and Women CX 1/2/3 races. Merch and medals for others.
Bacon Ridge etiquette
Pets on leashes are welcome—please clean up after them. Bacon Ridge is a public park, so please respect the venue and leave it cleaner than you found it.
Support the trails
Add an optional donation to Mid-Atlantic Off-Road Enthusiasts (MORE) during checkout to support trail building, stewardship, and advocacy throughout the region.

EventNotes:
About Kids Bike League

Kids Bike League is a program of the nonprofit Georgia Hi-Lo Trail, Inc. Our mission is to empower Georgia’s next generation of leaders through off-road cycling by fostering outdoor exploration, environmental stewardship, self-confidence, teamwork, and community engagement. Learn more at KidsBikeLeague.org.

Kids Bike League is committed to our belief that every child deserves the opportunity to explore outdoors, discover their potential, and connect with their community through the joy of cycling. All children are welcome at Kids Bike League regardless of their family’s ability to pay. For information about scholarship opportunities, contact Kids Bike League Director of Programming, Alden Strandburg.

Understanding Bikes & Gear

Kids Bike League supplies bikes and helmets to participants who do not have access to their own bike. 

Participants are welcome to bring their own bikes. Bikes must be in safe working order (brakes functioning, tires inflated, handlebars and seat secure). Coaches can help inspect bikes and provide alternatives when bikes are unsafe.

All participants are required to wear helmets when riding. Participants are also encouraged to bring helmets if available. Kids Bike League will provide helmets for participants when needed.

Preparing to Join a Ride

What to Wear

  • Wear comfortable clothing, with socks and closed-toed shoes.

What to Bring

  • Bring medications necessary for allergies or other potential medical emergencies (e.g. inhalers, epinephrine) .

Ride Dates & Locations

  • A complete list of ride dates and locations is available on KidsBikeLeague.org.

ZAC Outdoors is beyond honored to host the annual Gravel Big Brutus race series here at Big Brutus. Big Brutus, located in West Mineral, Kansas, is one of the most iconic landmarks in the Midwest and home to the “Worlds Largest” electric mining shovel that bears its name. As one of the largest shovels of its kind ever built, it stands as a monument to the region’s rich coal mining heritage. Set against a backdrop of rugged terrain and scenic rural roads, the area offers a premier gravel adventure characterized by rolling hills and a course that honors the hardworking history and larger-than-life legacy of Southeast Kansas. Plus, what better starting and finishing line than the worlds largest electric shovel??

EventNotes:
Galbraith Gravity Racing (GGR)-South

GGR-South is a satellite team through a partnership with the Bainbridge Island Mountain Bike Club (BIMBC) and GGR in Bellingham.  GGR South is based in Bainbridge Island for students ages up to 18 years old and focused on downhill and enduro mountain bike racing. Registration will open in the next couple of weeks for the fall season. Look for another email with the registration link.  Also, see https://bainbridgemountainbiking.org/ggr-south for details on the program. 

 

Fall 2026 Schedule

GGR South fall 2026 schedule  includes Monday, Wednesday, and Saturday practices with a couple of exceptions. In general week day practices will be at Port Gamble and Strawberry Hill Bike Park. Saturday practices include various locations including Capital Forest, Port Gamble and Snoqualmie.  A copy of the spring schedule can be found in the following link.  
 

Carpooling for practices and group rides will be offered as space is available. Parents and volunteer coaches are needed to register with GGR and join the team on group rides. Parents are expected to volunteer to help with group rides, carpools and fundraising. The program is only as good as the volunteers in the program. Please register as an adult volunteer at GGR registration and complete the SafeSport or Washington State Student Cycling League requirements. 

 

Coaching

Practices will include professional coaching by Jason Gainey, from Dirt Craft Mtb and student coaches that have gone through the GGR coaches training. The training will help students develop descending bike skills and learn fundamentals.

 

Safety Equipment

Crashing happens and wearing safety equipment will help keep you riding. Students are required to wear a full face helmet designed for downhill riding. Students are strongly encouraged to wear knee pads, elbow pads, chest protector, neck brace, gloves and glasses or goggles.

 

Discounts

Registered GGR-South students and volunteer coaches are eligible for discounts on numerous brands: Troy Lee Designs, Ride Concepts, Specialized, SRAM, Evil, Transition, Schwalbe, and more. 


Races

GGR South participates in the NW Cup, Race Cascadia , and GGR Galbraith Grassroots Gravity Series race series. The races are a full weekend of practice, racing, and fun! GGR is a race focused bike club and students are required to race a minimum of one race in the fall.  

 

GGR Jerseys

GGR 2026 jerseys are distributed in the spring.  However, let us know if you need a jersey so we can see if we have inventory with a size that fits you. 


RSVP & Questions about GGR South

Please let us know if you intend to register for GGR South in fall by emailing aclaiborne17@yahoo.com so we can plan ahead of the spring season.  


Please contact Lloyd Dixon ladixon2012@gmail.com

 or Aaron Claiborne aclaiborne17@yahoo.com with any questions about the upcoming season.   

 

Registration Team Fees

Registration will open in the next several weeks and we will send a follow up email with the registration link.  The cost for the fall season is $400.  

 

**Registration fees do not cover race fees, and bike park lift tickets.**

No recumbents, or e-bikes allowed.  

Ride safe and have a great time!
